newsitem.title: GERMANY: AIR INDIA PLANS EUROPE FREIGHTER, COMBI FLIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: AIR INDIA PLANS EUROPE FREIGHTER, COMBI FLIGHTS.

text.p: Air India said it will expand airfreight capacity between India and Europe substantially this summer with new freighter and combi flights.

From June 1, the carrier will fly Boeing 747-300 Combi flights twice-weekly to Paris and weekly to Amsterdam with Frankfurt stopovers on all three flights, the airline's Germany cargo sales manager, Ruediger Brasche, said.
From July 1, a B747-200 freighter will operate on Saturdays from Paris via Frankfurt to India, he added.
But the Frankfurt stopover on the twice-weekly Bombay-Chicago flight would be switched to London from end-May, he said.
"We are gradually returning to our old schedule. Sixty percent of capacity is reserved for Germany," Brasche told Reuters.
Air India would have 100 tonnes worth of weekly capacity from Germany compared to 30 tonnes now, he added.
The airline dropped loss-making freighter flights to Europe last year, industry sources said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax: 5017
